metadata.title: Cooperative optimization of neural-network-based diffraction simulations and benchtop spatial light modulators
metadata.abstract: The integration of neural networks and differentiable scalar wave optics has facilitated a modern approach to the design of optical systems, where simulation and optimization are carried out concurrently. These techniques encode the equations of wavefront propagation and modulation directly as layers of a neural network where the forward pass carries out simulation and the backward pass carries out optimization using the backpropagation algorithm. While this allows standard optical optimization as well as classifier-driven optimization of diffractive optics, it suffers from the ubiquitous simulation-to-reality gap. Identifying, characterizing, and ultimately reducing this simulation-to-reality gap is an ever-present objective – as the adage goes, “all models are wrong, some are useful.” To this end, this work extends recent advancements in physics-aware training where an optimizable physical device is used alongside in-silico simulation. By comparing the simulation output with the measured result from the physical device, an additional error term is introduced to the optimization objective. metadata.title: Ultracompact and efficient on-chip diffractive neural networks through physics-constrained dual-optimization
metadata.abstract: On-chip diffractive optical neural networks (OC-DONNs) on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platforms face significant inconsistencies between scalar diffraction training models and vector electromagnetic simulations. Existing solutions using slot groups, large metaline spacing, or auxiliary networks reduce integration density or increase computational overhead. We propose a dual-optimization approach combining Gaussian-smoothing diffractive neural networks (GS-DONN) with incident angle correction. Our physics-based method employs Gaussian filtering to suppress near-field coupling while incorporating spatially-varying transmission coefficients for oblique incidence. Requiring no training datasets, it adds only O(T·L·N·log N) computational complexity while maintaining robust performance across varying material properties and fabrication tolerances. The approach improves mode conversion fidelity from 34.91% to 98.10% with 93.39% mode purity. A three-layer GS-DONN achieves 96.67% accuracy on Iris classification. Remarkably, it maintains 97.77% fidelity at 20 μm layer separation, enabling high-density integration with complete physical interpretability.
